categories.main_business_segments: Taihei Dengyo operates primarily in two business segments: Construction Works and Maintenance Works. The Construction Works segment focuses on the installation and modification of power generation facilities (thermal, nuclear), steel plants, environmental protection, and chemical plants, including related electrical and instrumentation work, insulation, painting, and plant dismantling. The Maintenance Works segment provides regular inspections, daily maintenance, and repairs for similar facilities, and also includes the company’s power generation business (notably biomass).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies center on large-scale plant construction and maintenance, with expertise in engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) for power plants. It emphasizes safety, quality control, and efficiency in construction and maintenance, utilizing detailed work procedures, on-site safety patrols, and continuous improvement in methods. R&D focuses on improving construction machinery and tools, developing new decontamination techniques for nuclear plant decommissioning, and advancing CO2 utilization in biomass power generation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Taihei Dengyo’s primary customers are major power equipment manufacturers (notably Mitsubishi Heavy Industries), electric power utilities, steel manufacturers, and operators of biomass and other industrial plants. The company also serves environmental facilities and chemical plants, with a strong focus on the energy and heavy industry sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are concentrated in Japan, with a nationwide network of nine branches covering all major regions. Internationally, it has subsidiaries and projects in the Philippines and Indonesia, and conducts some business in Hong Kong and other parts of Asia. Over 98% of sales are domestic, with overseas sales primarily in Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: Taihei Dengyo operates as a midstream and downstream contractor in the supply chain, providing engineering, construction, installation, and maintenance services for large-scale industrial and power generation facilities. It acts as a key subcontractor for major equipment manufacturers and utilities, and also procures and manages subcontractors and suppliers for its projects.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, the company is focused on supporting Japan’s energy transition, balancing stable energy supply with decarbonization. R&D priorities include safety and productivity improvements, CO2 utilization in biomass power, and new decontamination technologies for nuclear decommissioning. The company is also advancing digital transformation (DX), green transformation (GX), and expanding its 'Green Project' integrating forestry, agriculture, and biomass power.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through contract-based construction and maintenance services for power plants and industrial facilities, using a project-based, lump-sum or progress-based billing model. The company also earns revenue from the operation of its own biomass power plants and from the sale of related equipment and parts.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other major Japanese engineering and construction firms specializing in power and industrial plants, such as Tokyo Energy & Systems, ENEOS Engineering, and Tokyo Enesys. Taihei Dengyo is positioned as a leading independent contractor with a strong reputation in the power sector, particularly in maintenance and nuclear-related projects, and maintains close relationships with major manufacturers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were ¥125.7 billion, with operating profit of ¥13.0 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥9.75 billion. The company has shown stable revenue with moderate growth in profits, a strong equity ratio (73.3%), and a workforce of approximately 1,900 employees. The company maintains a robust financial position with significant cash reserves and low leverage.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Taihei Dengyo differentiates itself through its deep expertise in power plant construction and maintenance, high safety and quality standards, and ability to handle complex projects such as nuclear plant decommissioning and biomass power integration. Its value proposition emphasizes reliability, technical excellence, and a comprehensive approach to supporting customers’ energy transition and sustainability goals.
